Stages 10 + 11 · the owner’s common flow, walked · Asks 21–25 · added 2026-10-11

A winter dome for six months: from the permit to every team’s schedule and budget, in one sitting

The owner’s words: “this is an example of a real world use case that is very common, the simpler and more streamlined we can make this the better … this is a real pain point for orgs at present.” Walked through the drawings with real numbers: four of the six steps found something the design didn’t do, and each is drawn below with its ask. What it takes, end to end: one permit form, one schedule window, one press to bill the teams, one send for review, one finalize. The teams’ schedules, Club tabs and budgets follow by themselves.

The owner’s flow, 2026-10-11

A winter dome for six months, walked step by step through the drawings

Lakeshore Dome (drawn, not seeded): Fields 1–4 full, 5–6 half · Sundays 8:00–11:00 a.m. · Oct 4 – Mar 28 · $27,000.00 · 8 teams.
StepWhat the admin does, in the drawingsWhat the walk found, and what is drawn
1 · The permit
Ask 21		Venue library › Permits › Add permit: Lakeshore Dome as issuer, reference W26-118, Oct 4 – Mar 28, one block (Fields 1–6, Sundays 8:00–11:00 a.m.), Dec 27 off, $27,000.00, the Dome Time budget line, the PDF. One form, about ten fields.Found: the permit had one cost, and a block named one facility. A dome prices its fields differently, and one block covers six fields. Drawn: a block takes several facilities; the permit says what each field costs (Full · Half · a share you type), so a full field is $72.00 an hour and a half field $36.00 (Ask 21).
2 · Six fields, two at half costThe venue’s six fields are entered once in the Venue library (Fields 1–4 and 5–6). Their size is the venue’s; their price is this permit’s, because next winter’s contract may price them differently.Holds as drawn, with step 1’s field prices on the permit, never on the venue.
3 · Sundays in 90-minute slots
Ask 22		Schedules › New schedule › Start from the permit (fills the dome, the fields, the dates, Sundays 8:00–11:00 a.m., Dec 27 off) · Slot length 90 min (12 slots a Sunday, 300 in all) · Senior 1 a week, Junior 2 · Generate · read By day · Save as a draft. About twelve presses.Found: no way to keep the half fields for the younger teams. Drawn: a rule, Fields by group (“Fields 5–6 · only for Junior”) (Ask 22).
4 · The cost to the teams, on a payment schedule
Ask 23		From the schedule’s page: Bill the teams opens New allocation filled in: the permit’s line and its $27,000.00, the split By the time each team got (at each field’s price), the payments Every two months from Oct 1, each payment the cost of that team’s Sundays in its two months. One press to open, one to create.Found: today a bill splits by count, percentage or amount, with one schedule of payments for every team; it can’t price each team’s time or make each payment that team’s months. Drawn: the split By the time each team got and payments that follow the schedule (Ask 23).
5 · Sent for review and approval
Ask 24		One Send for review carries both: each coach sees their Sundays and their bill, and answers Looks good or Ask for a change by the reply date. The admin reads the replies on the schedule’s page, makes the one swap 15U AA asked for, and presses Finalize and send.Found: the drawn send had no review step (ruled 10-08: a club slot is the club’s own booking). Drawn: an optional review round that never blocks: unanswered teams are listed, and the admin finalizes when ready (Ask 24).
6 · Teams’ schedules and budgets
Ask 25		On Finalize: each team’s Sundays land as practices from the club’s schedule (specimen 11), the bill lands on its Money › Club tab with its three payments, and the team’s Budget shows the club’s bill.Found: the team’s Budget never reads the club’s bills, so a coach who planned Dome Time at $10,000.00 keeps that guess beside a $2,700.00 bill. Drawn: the Budget reads the club’s bill on its word, and one press lets the coach use it (Ask 25, D1 respected: the club never writes the team’s book).

The figures, which all add up: 25 Sundays × 3 hours × 6 fields = 450 field-hours; a half field counts half, so the $27,000.00 buys 375 full-field hours at $72.00. 90-minute slots make 12 a Sunday and 300 in all: each Senior team gets one full field a week (25 slots, $2,700.00), each Junior team one full and one half (50 slots, $4,050.00); 4 × $2,700.00 + 4 × $4,050.00 = $27,000.00. Payments Every two months from Oct 1: 9 Sundays, then 8, then 8, so a Senior team pays $972.00, $864.00, $864.00 and a Junior team $1,458.00, $1,296.00, $1,296.00.

Stages 10 + 11 · formatting check

The drawings against the benchmark, and the places the rules pull apart

Every frame was checked against the Coaches Portal’s written rules and the calendar recipe before it went on this page. The second table lists where two rules disagree, so you can rule them instead of finding them.

Checked before you saw it

Every drawing against the portal’s written rules and the calendar recipe

RuleHow the drawings meet itResult
Page frameEvery club page centred at one of the portal’s two widths: 1200 for the Venue library, Schedules and a schedule’s grid; windows at the kit’s 640, the generator’s 800, a question’s 416.Held
TitlesPage titles in the condensed display face; a back arrow one level up (a schedule → Schedules); no club name above a title (2026-10-01).Held
TablesHeadings in the display face, upper case, secondary ink; figures right and tabular; the name is the link with one chevron, the row opens from anywhere; no links or buttons in cells; band rows say a state once.Held
One lime a screenAdd permit · New schedule · Generate drafts · Save the draft · Send · Send the changes: one each. On a changed schedule the line’s Send steps aside for the callout’s Send the changes.Held
FiguresA permit’s cost and use, the fairness figures: the joined band (2026-10-08), never cards with gaps.Held
RecordsA permit and a venue read first and edit whole; rare doors (Renew, Delete, Archive, Hand back, Lock, Clear) end the body; Delete red and only when nothing depends on it; no Done.Held
Create asksAdd permit and New schedule have Cancel and a create button; editing a permit autosaves; a sent schedule’s changes wait for Send the changes, the ruled exception for a change that tells people.Held
ExportOne button, Excel first, one line naming the file, above what it exports; Calendar only once a schedule is sent.Held
Calendar recipeMonday first (C2); “Jan 4 – 10, 2027” (C8); a range on a club-wide page (R9); the team’s colour (R4); the zone said once (C10); today in words when the week holds it (C7); the phone week one frame a day (C13); a cancelled or handed-back booking struck through and never hidden (C9).Held
CalloutsWhite with a coloured edge (tinted panels retired 2026-09-21): Nobody to send to, the changes, a line’s not allocated.Held
WordsEvery sentence drawn is a draft for /marketing; “From Winter dome 2026–27 · the club’s schedule” is Ask 16.For /marketing
Where rules pull apart

Said out loud rather than picked silently

The pullWhat the drawings do
The generator’s frame vs the record standardA schedule’s page is a record the club keeps, but it is not a window: it is a page (a grid needs 1200). The record standard (read first, the pencil) is for windows; a schedule’s settings reopen in the generator window from Tools › Settings…, which asks before it regenerates.
“The Timeline’s shape” vs the TimelineThe ruled words and the built Timeline disagree on the axes (finding P11-01). Drawn to specimen 4, which the owner saw; Ask 12 settles it and the standard’s R3 is reworded after.
A held change vs autosaveEditing autosaves (2026-09-24), but a change that tells families is held and asks (2026-10-09). A sent schedule’s edits are the second kind: they wait for Send the changes (Ask 14).
Found, not this stage’sA budget line’s window still has Done in its foot, which record windows lost on 2026-10-09 (Stage 3’s to remove). The tournament’s Round-robin generator has no Cancel beside Generate drafts (the tournament redesign’s, as a finding).
The /design review · 2026-10-10

Seventeen drawing changes, made before you saw the drawings

Every frame read against the written rules at 1440 and 390, Warm and Dark. Proposals until ruled; nothing written to the design log.
What the review foundThe rule, and what changedWhere
Phone lists drawn as separate cardsPermits, Schedules and a schedule By team on a phone were white cards with gaps. The 2026-09-29 phone-list ruling (standard §3.10.8): one frame, band rows, hairlined rows, the corner chevron; a separate card only for a record of labelled lines. Redrawn as one frame.Specimens 1, 13
A coloured rail on list rowsThe By team phone rows carried the team’s colour as a rail on the row’s edge, a calendar-cell idiom that a list never draws (§3.10.7). Now the team’s swatch in the lead-mark slot.Specimen 13
Two lead marks on one rowThe team picker (Who) and the Send window led each row with a tick and a team swatch. One lead mark (§3.10.7): a form row leads with its tick. The swatch is gone there.Specimens 4, 9
Table cells top-alignedEvery cell of every table is centred (§3.4, 2026-09-16); the drawings’ tables aligned to the top. Centred.Specimens 1, 4, 8
An explanation under a read factThe venue window read “Bookings contact” with a sentence under it. Read rows are bare facts (owner, 2026-10-08, the Fiscal year window); the sentence belongs to the field’s hint in the edit form. Removed from the read.Specimen 1
A second door in a read window’s footThe calendar’s read window gained “Open the schedule” beside its one door. The foot’s one door is the window’s purpose (C12; 2026-10-09); the schedule’s name in the From row is now that door, for the people who build schedules.Specimen 12
The coach’s sentence in the wrong place“Only the club can move or remove this practice.” sat inside the From line; the mirror puts its own sentence at the body’s end, where Delete would be. Moved there, under Hand back, at 1440 and 390.Specimen 11
A create form without CancelNew schedule’s step 1 foot had only Generate drafts. A form that creates keeps Cancel beside its button (2026-10-09). Added.Specimen 4
One empty day, drawn two waysFriday read “No time held” and Sunday “—”, though both are days with no time held. One mark, the recipe’s empty day (C7): “—”.Specimens 6, 7, 10
A unit on every row (2026-10-11)Who, and how much under A set number a week repeated “a week” on every team row under an “A WEEK” heading. The heading says it once; a group row keeps “each”, which says how its figure spreads. Percentages keep “%”, as New allocation’s rows do.Specimen 4
A day’s slots as two-line rows (2026-10-11)The drafts’ By day list first drew each slot as a two-line booking row (team over lane). A row that holds one line is compact (§3.1): time, team, lane on one line, which halves a 354-slot list.Specimen 5
A menu that floated (2026-10-11)The drafts’ Export menu was drawn over the rows; a menu hangs from the button that opens it.Specimen 5
“From the club” on a bill (2026-10-11)The coach’s review window opened “From the club · Winter dome · Sundays”: in the coach’s Money that phrase already means money the club pays the team (finding P11-03), and this window carries a bill. It reads “The club’s proposal”.Specimen 14
A frame that showed two states at once (2026-10-11)The team’s Budget after Finalize drew the line already at $2,700.00 while the callout still offered “Use $2,700.00”. The frame now shows the moment before the coach answers; the tag says what Use does.Specimen 14
Whole dollars outside a month grid (2026-10-11)Fair shares counted the bill in whole dollars (“$2,700”). Whole-dollar notation is ruled for the month grids only (2026-10-06); money elsewhere carries its cents.Specimen 14
Capital headings on a PDF (2026-10-11)The schedule PDF’s table headings were drawn in capitals; the house PDFs (the tournament schedule, the year-end report) set them in sentence case.Specimen 15
A foot that counted the wrong thing (2026-10-11)New schedule’s foot said “354 slots for 8 teams.”, the slots the time holds, not what Generate hands out. The tournament’s foot counts what it will make: “288 slots for 8 teams.”Specimen 4

Held as drawn, with the reason: the Permits view’s year pill follows the view switch rather than leading the line (C4 lets a scope lead only when it doesn’t depend on the view; only Permits has a year). Band rows sit on the paper tone with the display face, as 6c’s ratified row list does. Filter pills keep 6b’s built height. The dimmed page under a window shows its own lime: it is the page, not a second lime in the window.

Stages 10 + 11 · not drawn

What the builds carry that no drawing shows

The plan’s §7 holds the build split and the expected migrations. This is the list each build prompt starts from.

The builds carry it

What no drawing shows

PartWhat it needs
The engineA time-allocation engine of its own: one-sided (a team asks for hours, not a matchup), measured in hours, prime time and nights, honouring locked slots and the rules. Not the tournament’s, which pairs two-sided games and penalises evenings (P11-02).
Writing the bookingsAt the send, once: one practice row per slot date on each team, carrying a link to its slot (as the mirror carries its game), never on read (P11-05). The server refuses a coach’s change to a club slot’s time, place or name, as the mirror does.
Shared slots and the clash ruleRows from one club slot never clash with each other (two teams sharing a lane), and the club calendar reads a shared slot as one booking with its teams (P11-04a).
Availability“Never on a team’s game day” reads each team’s whole schedule (away games on typed places included), not the clash pool, which holds the club’s venues only (P11-04c).
SeasonsA slot lands in the team’s running season at the send; starting a team’s next season carries its upcoming club slots into the new one (Ask 15, P11-06).
Hand-backIts route, its series question, the builders’ notice, the slot’s “handed back” state; the family feed stops carrying it.
SendingThe reminders’ pattern carried over: the preview, a claim in the database against a double send, reply-to the sender, the demo club’s guard; colleague mail for staff, the family choke point for any family send (Stage 7); a Your club notice; the send log table.
PermitsThe permit and block tables (one model), dates off, an org document store (none exists), the venue’s bookings contact, the quiet line beside the pair rule on every Where form, the use read over the one pool, the budget line’s Pays for, Renew.
PlansThe scheduler’s feature key (League Plus and both Club bands), and Ask 4’s answer for permits, each with the Plan & Pricing Facts doc in the same change (/billing, /strategy).
ExportsThe export catalog entries: a schedule’s Excel, PDF and Calendar; a permit’s use. The PDF drawn in the browser, as every PDF is today.
The feed (6d)Every club slot in the team’s feed; a cancelled one marked cancelled, not dropped; a handed-back one gone; the club’s clock.
GatesA guard that there is one model of time (no second slot table); screen guards for both stages; the permit’s Held / Booked / Unused band recomputed from rows (the money-arithmetic gate’s pattern); check:layout in both themes.
HelpVenue library › Permits; a permit’s use; Schedules; New schedule; the grid; Send; a coach’s club slot and Hand back — through /docs at build.
House league (Stage 9)The practice link and creator; the scheduler’s house-league writer (move, cancel) past today’s owner/league-admin gate through the scheduler’s own rule; the Practices view’s caption; league admins in the send.

Not in the first cut (proposed): requesting or paying for permits through the platform; municipal integrations; public booking; families requesting or swapping slots; coaches trading slots; a public schedule page; paying for time per slot; any optimizer beyond the rules drawn; an email attachment. (The split by hours joined the first cut on 2026-10-11, as Ask 23’s Bill the teams.)

Stage 11c · where it stands

New schedule asks a lot before it says anything, and two things a club wants have no setting

Read before drawing: what the window draws, what the generator does with a shared slot, and why every Sunday comes out the same.

On this screen:
Read first

What New schedule and the generator do today

From the code, the dome’s walk (§300) and the owner’s capture.
PartWhat the code does (read 2026-10-12)What it means for the clubFinding
Teams at onceOne number for the whole schedule. Every slot gets that many seats, and any team can take any seat (the generator’s seats; the slot window refuses a third team in a two-team slot).Two at once makes every team share, seniors included. “Juniors share, seniors don’t” has no setting.
A shared slot’s costBill the teams splits a slot’s minutes evenly among its teams (Bill’s priced minutes).Already half each when two teams share: the owner’s ruling (2026-10-12) is how Bill works today.
A shared slot’s fairnessThe generator counts each team the slot’s whole minutes, and each seat as one slot toward a share.Fair shares and the bill disagree the moment teams share: a team sharing every slot reads as getting double the time it pays for.
Which slot a team getsEach week leans on what the team had before: the same facility, the same start, the same day (the continuity cost).The owner’s capture: every Sunday identical, 14U AA always Field 1 at 8:00 a.m.
Rotating“Rotate it weekly” moves PRIME TIME only, and only where prime time is set; the “Prime time rotated” draft does the same. With no prime time (the dome) nothing ever moves.Spreading early and late, field to field, has no setting at all.
Prime timeIts hours and Keep / Rotate live in Rules; how it is shared lives in Who, and how much, and appears only once hours are set and the split is By percentage.One idea, two cards, and a control that appears in an earlier card because of a choice in a later one.
Rules, openedFive kinds drawn every time: three headings with Add doors, two “No limit” dropdowns, prime time, three ticks. About thirteen controls before the club has a single rule.The folded line already writes rules as sentences (“9U AA, 11U AA finish by 8:00 p.m.”); the open card does not.
A half facilityA permit’s half field counts half, for the fairness swap and for the bill (its weight).Sharing a half field would make a quarter. Not drawn; the build’s rule (Not drawn).

Three owner questions, one window: sharing (“certain teams share a field but not all”), spreading (“sometimes the early one and sometimes the later one, sometimes Field 1 and sometimes Field 3”), and reading (“is there a better way to group and organize this page”). Ruled before drawing (owner, 2026-10-12): a shared slot counts as half a facility from a cost perspective.

The /design review (2026-10-12) — changes made to these drawings, proposals until ruled

#What the review foundWhat changed
D1The schedule’s page still said “Times in Eastern time.” on its toolbar.Removed from both grid drawings: the owner took it off this page today (design log 2026-10-12).
D2Remove this rule was red, a delete.Ink, the record’s undoable door (RecordAction): nothing is saved until Generate drafts, as the Divisions step’s “Remove this division” (2026-10-12).
D3The required asterisk was red.Ink, as the product draws it (the club kit’s required mark inherits the label’s colour).
D4A shared slot carried a “Shared” mark: a third line in every shared chip, making Fields 3 and 4 taller than the rest.Dropped. Two names stacked and the edge in both teams’ colours already say it; the slot window and a screen reader name it.
D5A faded slot was 0.32.0.35, the grid’s own fade for the Team filter.
D6Add a rule’s menu opened with a heading that repeated its button.Dropped: a menu names a group only when there is something to tell apart (2026-10-09).
D7The filtered team’s chips wore an olive ring.Dropped: the built Team filter dims the other slots and draws nothing on the picked team’s; the drawing shows what the product does.

Kept, and why: rules as sentences match the folded line, so open and closed read alike; the foot’s count sits at its left (2026-10-12); Each team’s time is a dropdown with its sentence under it, as Event settings ruled the same day for a one-value choice; every frame reads in Dark. Raised, not changed: the drawing kit’s required asterisk is red in every Stages 10 + 11 drawing while the product’s is ink; fixed here for 11c only.

Stage 11c · not drawn

What the build carries that no drawing shows

The shape of the build if the asks are ruled as recommended. Nothing here is decided by drawing it.

For the build

Settings, generator, measures, words, walks

PartWhat the build carries
The settingsTeams at once becomes a rule list (Sharing a facility: teams, groups, how many). A schedule saved with Teams at once above 1 reads as one rule naming every team, so nothing saved changes meaning. Each team’s time is one more setting; the prime-time Keep / Rotate setting folds into it.
The generatorA slot’s seats depend on who sits in them: a team outside every sharing rule takes the whole slot; teams in one rule fill its seats together. Paired whenever a partner is free (Ask 2). Moved around adds a cost for last week’s start and facility, every slot, the way prime-time rotation does today; nights keep their pull (Ask 4).
What a shared slot countsHours toward By percentage and Evenly count half a facility; A set number a week still counts practices (2 a week = 2 practices). The fairness swap already weighs a half field; it weighs a shared seat the same way (Ask 3).
A half facility sharedA permit’s half field shared by two would be a quarter each. The build refuses it (a sharing rule uses the full facilities) or counts it as a quarter; recommended: refuse, said in the rule’s sentence.
The slot windowChange team on a shared slot names both teams; the refusal for a third team in a two-team slot reads the rule’s number.
Measures and Fair sharesHours replaces Prime when there is no prime time; Early and Fields show when the schedule moves teams around; each draft says how evenly early and late fell.
WordsRule sentences, the menu’s lines, Each team’s time and its two sentences, the Sharing hint: /marketing at the build.
HelpNew schedule: the time / who and how much / rules; a section on sharing a facility and on moving teams around (/docs at the build).
WalksOne walk per purpose: the regrouped window; a sharing rule end to end (the page, Fair shares, the bill); Moved around end to end (the drafts, the page). §300’s walks are unaffected until the build lands; W1–W2 then read “Permit” and the regrouped Rules.
PhonesNew schedule is desk only (P11-10); a phone reads the schedule, where a shared slot is one row naming both teams.
Stage 11d · where it stands

A hand-back gives the time back at once and the money back to nobody

Read before drawing: what Hand back does, what the page does after it, and where the money it frees ends up.

On this screen:
Read first

What a hand-back does to the time and the money today

From the code, walk §300 (W7–W10) and dev’s rows after them.
PartWhat the code does (read 2026-10-12)What it means for the clubFinding
Handing backThe coach picks which practices (this one, this and the rest, all of them) and presses Hand back. It lands at once: the team leaves the slots, a practice the coach never touched is deleted (one with notes or attendance stays, struck through), the builders get a bell. Nothing about money is asked or said.A coach giving back four paid-for Sundays has no way to say “and we’d like the money back”.
The page afterA hand-back marks the schedule Changed since sent, on purpose: build question B settles a hand-back’s money at the next Send the changes. But the page offers Send the changes only when the club changed a team’s time, so after a hand-back alone the callout says “Send the changes…” with no button (walk §300 W10, captured below).A dead end, and a false sentence: the team already has the change, the coach made it.
The money a hand-back freesAt the next Send the changes the team is measured again: 21 Sundays instead of 25 makes 15U AA owed $432.00 back. The figure is written to the send log, but a changes send emails only teams whose practices it changes, and the hand-back already removed them.The club owes 15U AA $432.00 by its own arithmetic, and nobody, the coach included, is ever told.
A bill after FinalizeA bill’s terms never change (Ask 7b): its shares, its payments, its teams have no writer. A team pays a bill or the club receives it; a request the coach files is the only way club money reaches a team, and paying the team never lowers what the team owes. No credit exists anywhere in club money.“What they owe just goes down” has nothing to write it with today. It is the new part of this stage.
Fair shares’ Bill columnFair shares prices each team’s time as it stands now: after the hand-back it reads 15U AA $2,268.00 (21 Sundays). The bill 15U AA got still reads $2,700.00 on its Money › Club.Two numbers for one team’s money, and nothing on the page says which is owed.
The club’s own changesWhen the club moves a team out of time (Send the changes), the team that loses it is told “15U AA is owed $108.00 back: its coach asks for it on Money › Club” (build question B, ruled 2026-10-11, “Bill gains, show losses”). The coach then files a request by hand.The same money settles two ways: a club move is told and left to the coach; a hand-back is told to nobody.

The owner’s direction (2026-10-12, from walk §300 W10): “for handing back, can we give the option to include money back (i.e. equivalent of requesting money) so then the club confirms the hand back, thus opening the time slot and also making a ‘payment request’ that they later have to action as ‘paid’ once they do it. If the money is still owing from the team the amount they owe just goes down by that amount and there is nothing for the club to further action.” What it changes on the record: build question B (2026-10-11) chose “nothing new enters the money loop”, because the club can’t put money into a team’s books unasked. The refund half keeps that reason: the coach’s ask is the coach’s own request. The “goes down” half is new: a credit. It lowers a debt; it gives no money. Ask 6 is that decision.

Stage 11d · not drawn

What the build carries that no drawing shows

The shape of the build if the asks are ruled as recommended. Nothing here is decided by drawing it.

For the build

The ask, the credit, the club’s own changes, words, walks

PartWhat the build carries
The askA hand-back with money is a pending ask: the slots, the scope chosen, the figure (the Sundays at the bill’s rate when asked), who asked and when. Its practices stay on the team’s schedule and in the family feed until the club answers. Withdraw removes it. Without the tick, Hand back is exactly today’s.
The request it carriesThe ask is a From-club, money-back request on the team’s season, filed under the bill’s own word, linked to the ask so it can’t be edited apart from it; it shows on both lists. It counts as an unanswered request for the season close-out (an unanswered request already blocks it).
A Sunday that arrives unansweredDrops out of the ask the day it starts, and its figure with it; an ask whose every Sunday has passed closes itself, and the coach is told (Ask 7).
AcceptOne step: the slots open (handed back by the team, as today’s hand-back), the practices leave the team’s schedule, the credit and any request to pay are written, the coach is told. Never sets Changed since sent (Ask 9).
The creditA new kind of row on the club↔team account: dated, against one bill, never more than what is left on it, applied to its latest unpaid payment first (a payment it fully covers reads Credited, not Paid). Reminders, Owed by the teams, the team statement, Money › Club, Budget vs. Actual on both sides, the club’s fiscal-year figures and the exports read billed less credited. A credit in a closed fiscal year is refused, as every write there is.
The request to payWhat the team had already paid becomes an accepted From-club request waiting in Payment requests, paid with the Approve window as built. The coach’s row reads “Accepted · the club pays it” until then.
The club’s own changesSend the changes credits a team that loses time (or makes a request to pay, if it has paid) under the same Bill the corrections switch; the changes email and the send log say it. Build question B’s owed-back line goes, and the hidden owed-back for a hand-back with it (S11D-03).
Fair sharesThe Bill column reads each team’s bill as billed less credited plus corrections, so it agrees with Money › Club; a team that handed time back without asking reads what it still pays, with a note.
WhoAsking: a coach who can use the team’s money (and can hand back). Answering: someone who holds the club’s Accounting. Builders without it see the ask on the schedule’s page without Answer.
Bells and emailThe ask (builders and Accounting holders), the answer (the team’s staff with money access), a withdrawn or lapsed ask. Words: /marketing at the build.
HelpThe coach’s Hand back with money back; the club answering it; credits on a bill and the statement (/docs at the build).
WalksOne purpose each: a coach asks and withdraws; the club accepts while the team owes (the credit on both sides); accepts after it paid (the request to pay); declines; a club move at Send the changes credits the loser; a plain hand-back leaves the page Final. W10b from §300, the correction money, rides with the last.

Product-manager brief

Club Tier Production Readiness

What it is

A staged programme that takes the Club plan from "built but never tested" to "a rep club can buy it, set it up, staff it, run a season on it and trust the numbers it shows the board." Each part of the offer is tackled, walked and signed off one at a time, in the order a real club meets them. House league is deliberately last so Club can be released to rep clubs that run no house league.

Why it matters

  • Club is the top of the pricing ladder and has never been validated against one real club. Every June pricing decision is still a hypothesis.
  • The club-admin side has been effectively static since June while the Coaches Portal got three months of intensive work. The two halves now disagree about money, seasons, venues and who can do what.
  • The June audit of the club president's journey found the oversight layer "part broken and part unguarded". Today's re-verification: of its 50 findings, 7 fixed, 6 partly, 4 superseded, 33 still open. Of the 27 staff-admin findings, 19 still open.
  • Every coach in a club is on a free Premium portal until September 2027. A club pays $219 a month only for what the club side gives it. That is exactly the side that has never been QA'd.

What the club sees and does differently when this is done

Buying and setting up. A club owner is provisioned (or buys) onto Club or Club · Association, sees the right price and trial, is walked through a club-shaped setup, and lands on a hub that leads with the club's own programs. Cancelling and coming back restores everything.

Staffing the board. The owner invites an admin who can see the club's modules, a treasurer and a registrar, from the Members screen, with roles that mean what the screen says. A volunteer who also coaches elsewhere can be invited.

Teams and coaches. The owner creates teams and program years, names coaches, and each coach lands in a populated Premium portal at no per-team charge. Starting and closing a season means the same thing on both sides. The president gets one oversight view of every team.

Money the board can repeat. The treasurer plans a budget for the club's year, allocates to teams, approves coach requests with a confirmation and a way back, and reads one board summary whose every figure is true by construction and guarded by a build check. Team money and club money are two clearly separated things; the club reads the coach's records rather than keeping a shadow copy.

A public face that leads with the rep program. Families find the teams, open tryouts and the club's colours. "Tryouts are open" takes them to the tryout. Unlisting from the directory no longer takes down the website.

Families. Household records read the same money the Money hub does, a changed guardian email follows the child, a merge stays merged, and the export says what it holds.

One venue book. Rep, house-league and tournament games read the same venues, and a diamond double-booked across modules is flagged.

The club’s schedules (added and ruled 2026-10-08). A scheduler for the club’s shared time: parameters in, a draft out, adjusted by hand, finalized, kept by name, summarized and sent to the people who need it. Drawn with permits; the first release waits for it; League Plus and both Club bands carry it alike.

One calendar (drawn and ratified 2026-10-10). Nine calendars, from the coach’s schedule to the family app, compared on a computer and a phone. One recipe for how a calendar reads (views, today, the toolbar, one booking row, one spelling for a day, nothing hidden), a register of what differs on purpose, the coach’s desk schedule and the club calendar redrawn, and three date defects fixed first. Every ask ruled as recommended, and built the same day: the coach’s schedule opens on today with one row of controls and Import inside Add Event, the club calendar lists bookings as rows and shows cancelled and postponed ones, and an admin’s view of a team’s schedule is the coach’s own screens, read-only. Eleven walks (§289) are on the QA tab; the Stage 10 + 11 session may open.

Permits and the club’s schedules (drawn 2026-10-10, ratified 2026-10-11: every question as recommended). The club records the permits and rentals it holds once, in the Venue library, and sees how much of each it uses. It hands that time to its teams with a scheduler: pick the time, tick the teams and split the time between them (evenly, a number a week, or by percentage, 60% to one group and 40% to another), generate ranked drafts, bill the teams for the time each got with payments that follow it, send it for review, adjust on a week grid that shows every open slot, and send it with a preview of who is told what. Coaches find the club’s slots on their team’s schedule and can hand one back. Changes are sent as changes. House league’s half is recommended to arrive with house league’s own stage.

Calendar feeds (drawn and ratified 2026-10-11; the club admin’s feed deferred). A coach subscribes once, from the Schedule’s Export at a desk or the calendar mark on a phone, and the team’s schedule stays current in their own calendar app: every event, the tryout days they run, the organizer’s games, cancelled ones kept and marked. A family subscribes from the team’s public page when the coach shares the schedule publicly; the family view’s own door waits for counsel. A club admin’s own feed is drawn and deferred: few would hold one, and it is the costliest to serve. One window serves all of them: pick the app, see what’s in it and how often it updates, see whether a calendar has read it, and reset the link. Today nobody receives a feed: no team shares its schedule publicly and no family can connect.

New schedule, round two (drawn and ratified 2026-10-12; built once the dome walk is complete). Three things a club asked of the scheduler while walking it. Some teams can share a facility while the rest keep one to themselves: name the teams (two young teams, or a whole group) and they are paired, each paying half, while today the only choice makes every team share. A club can have each team’s time move around, early one week and late the next, field to field, instead of every week the same. And the window reads as three questions (what time, who gets how much, what the club won’t allow), with each rule written as a sentence and nothing shown for a rule the club hasn’t added.

A hand-back that asks for money back (drawn 2026-10-12; nine asks open). When a coach gives club time back today, the time is handed back at once and the money it frees reaches nobody: the club’s own arithmetic says the team is owed it, and nobody is told. Now the coach can tick “ask for the money back” when handing time back. The club accepts or declines. Accepting opens the time and either takes the money off what the team still owes or, for what the team has already paid, puts a payment in the club’s list to record when it is paid. When the club itself moves a team out of time, the money comes back the same way. The one new thing in club money is a credit: what a team owes can go down without the bill it was sent ever changing.

Tested and documented. A Club fixture and browser suite, admin screens in the layout sweep, help that describes today's screens, marketing that promises only what exists.

Who benefits

Club owners and presidents (the buyer), treasurers, registrars and admins (the roles the plan sells but the screen cannot assign today), coaches in a club (their portal stays; the club side stops contradicting it), and families. Standalone Premium coaches are unaffected.

Trade-offs

  • Fix the club side to read the coach's records rather than rebuilding both money models — the coach side has three months of hardening and build gates; the club's copy has neither.
  • Permits and a club-wide calendar are new features, not readiness items. Both are decided: the club calendar is in the first release (D5), and permits are Stage 10, which the release waits for (D4, amended 2026-09-25). Because Stage 10 sits on Stage 6’s venue book and clash check, the release waits for Stage 6 too. The risk left is size, not a decision.
  • Families P3 is not release-gating; its four serious defects are.
  • House league last, and no new plan needs inventing — League Plus already is the standalone plan.

Success criteria

  1. One real rep club (or the fixture standing in) completes the nine-point exit definition with the owner watching; every stage's QA walk is on the ledger as passed.
  2. Every board-facing figure has a build gate, and the same number cannot be computed two ways on two screens.
  3. Every June audit finding routed to Club is fixed or explicitly superseded — none open.
  4. Club and Club · Association can be bought in-product, the gate flip is one decision away, and the marketing surfaces promise only what exists.
Full plan — condensed

Ten stages, one exit definition

The full ledger lives in the plan file

CLUB_TIER_PRODUCTION_READINESS_PLAN.md carries every finding with its code anchor (sections 4A–4I), the eleven rulings (§5), sequencing (§7), build gates (§8), the release checklist (§9) and the June-audit register (§11). This tab is the reading version.

Release-ready for a rep club means

  1. Buy or be provisioned onto Club with the right price, trial and comp state; cancel and come back with everything restored.
  2. Staff the board — owner, an admin who sees the modules, a treasurer, a registrar — including volunteers who coach elsewhere.
  3. Create teams and program years, name coaches, every coach lands in a populated Premium portal; a season starts and closes the same way on both sides.
  4. Plan a budget for a club year, allocate, receive requests, mark money received, and read one board summary that is true by construction and guarded.
  5. Show a public face that leads with the rep program.
  6. Know its families — same money as the Money hub, merges that hold, emails that follow the child.
  7. Keep one venue book every module reads.
  8. Coexist with tournaments — the club's own team enters its own event, the mirror keeps the coach's schedule true.
  9. Be tested: fixture, browser suite, layout sweep, current help, truthful marketing.
  10. Hold its permits (ruled in 2026-09-25): the club records the field, diamond or ice permits it holds, every module's scheduling reads them, and a permit's cost sits in the budget. Stage 10, and the release waits for it.

Stages

Stage 0 — Ground truth

Fixes + fixture + rulings · no mockup · walk §A

Seed the Club fixture (six teams, three program-year states, real coach memberships, guardians shared across teams, a budget year, allocations, requests, a tournament with the club's own team). Fix the dead-control class in one sweep: the two money-entry controls, the audit log, the dead rep-team links, the reminder-button roles, the tryouts card. Ship the security fix-now on its own: the house-league tenant-boundary hole, the archive org check, rate limits, escaped emails. Rule D1, D2, D8. Walk it end to end. Exit: every club screen opens for owner, admin and treasurer without a wall.

Stage 1 — The club shell

Provision · buy · cancel · return · roles · nav · settings · walk §B

Prerequisite (owner, 2026-09-25): the Admin Design Continuity foundation lands first, so every admin screen, tournament screens included, already follows the account theme in both palettes before the club shell is rebuilt on it. Mockups: a plan-aware hub (what the club runs first; a president's morning brief), the phone bar and More sheet for a club, Members with board roles and a coach row, the billing page for a Club with both band prices and a prorated move to Club · Association (D7), Org Settings that name the public-site switch honestly, the club onboarding checklist, the audit log. Roles per D8; the hub decides "tournament-only" from the plan; the membership policy stops counting coach rows; comp scoped to the promo plans; reactivate restores everything; one gating source; the coach portal checks the plan on downgrade. 1b · Buying Club and Club · Association (ruled 2026-09-25): both band prices published, a real Club purchase on the billing page, and the Club ↔ Club · Association move as a prorated subscription change rather than a second checkout; no Founding Season banner ever speaks for Club.

Stage 2 — Rep teams & the coach bridge

Rulings D10 + the club season lifecycle first · walks §C §D, Shared Book §1.16, host-own-team

An "Invite a coach" door that writes the membership and sends the mail. The club gets the same season roll the standalone portal has, invoked by the admin; whether a Draft year may run beside the Active one is Ask 1 (drawn 2026-09-28, recommending one model: tryouts on the working season). A team page with edit and a "what the club sees" panel (coach in place · roster · next event · documents · money owed — the franchise health board). Finish the ownership-transfer routine so a standalone coach's portal can join the club without losing its data, with a gate that keeps it complete. One rule for roster counts and one for records.

Stage 3 — Club money (four parts)

D1 + D2 applied · walks §E §F §G · new build gates

3a bookkeeping core and the allocation/request loop: team ledgers read-only and labelled, transfers void both sides, payees managed; allocations with true overdue and team names; confirm on every money move, a way back, one atomic write per transfer, the coach's meaning visible to the club. 3b budget with many allocations per line and next year plannable; Budget vs. Actual with actuals by line; one headroom definition; the board summary (club position · receivables · team-held money labelled · one export); Budget and Summary in the sidebar. 3c the club year: label + start month, year-end lock and carry, ledgers archived. Gates: the summary's arithmetic recomputed from rows, one definition per figure, transfer atomicity. 3a drawn 2026-09-30 (Mockups → Stage 3a): seven specimens, a re-read of every money row, five new findings and six asks, all ratified the same day as recommended (hub v22). Redrawn the same day to the coach’s Money format, with the frame posed as two options (Ask 2). 3b drawn 2026-10-05 (Mockups → Stage 3b): a re-read of every row 3b owns, each figure’s one definition, six specimens (the Budget · Budget vs. Actual · the board summary · a team’s money · the shared-payee report · the coach’s side), a formatting check and a Not-drawn list; nine asks on the Decisions tab (Ask 5, the Months view, added 2026-10-06 at the owner's question), all ratified 2026-10-06 as recommended, with the two coach month-grid fixes; build prompts CLUB_TIER_STAGE3B_SERVER_PROMPT.md then CLUB_TIER_STAGE3B_SCREENS_PROMPT.md. A /design pass the same day redrew the places the drawings had drifted from the coach's screens (listed on the Formatting check). 3b built 2026-10-06 (the server session committed 26277b5f; the screens session committed baefbe7d (the rulings) and ad957b4e (the build) the same day, after /simplify, /review, check:layout in both themes and /design at 1440 and 390): eleven walks, ledger §271, on the QA tab; a twelfth, the Ledger’s Item column (2026-10-07), is ledger §279. 3c mockup item added 2026-10-07 (the owner, in the §271 walk): New allocation, redrawn. Today Allocate leaves the line’s window for a three-step page in the old Rep Teams style, and Create lands on the allocation’s own page, so the treasurer goes back to the Budget and reopens the line by hand. Two shapes to draw: A, the line’s window turns into the allocation form on one screen and returns to the line with the new allocation listed (recommended); B, a one-screen page in the portal’s format that returns to the line. One form for both doors, the line and the Allocations tab. 3c opens this form anyway (open seasons only, the year’s name), so it is redrawn once. The full item is in the plan, §6 Stage 3c. And a design review added the same day (the owner, at W10): what the teams recorded paying a shared payee opens a page of its own from the payee’s window. Recommended: it becomes the body of that window, which reads first and edits whole under one pencil (the window opens straight into an editable name today); the alternative keeps the page and opens it from the Payees list. Full item in the plan, §6 Stage 3c. 3c drawn 2026-10-07 (Mockups → Stage 3c): where the year is read today (about a dozen places, not one), Ask 1 (a closed year read in place, a departure from the coach’s one-page ruling, argued on its reasons), and eight specimens: setting the club’s year (the year that changes is the next one, short), every money page reading a named year, closing a year (warns, never blocks; a closed year locked in place; Reopen with a reason), the year that opens, the annual meeting’s papers (against last year, the year-end report), New allocation in the line’s window, the payee window reading first with its report inside, and the coach’s side (an unpaid bill must not leave the Club tab at a roll). Ratified 2026-10-07, every ask as recommended, with Ask 9: the club’s year is its fiscal year, on the club side only. Build prompts: CLUB_TIER_STAGE3C_SERVER_PROMPT.md, then CLUB_TIER_STAGE3C_SCREENS_PROMPT.md. 3d added 2026-10-08 (the owner, after the §283 walks): the last money pages become windows. The Payees list opens over the Ledger, as the coaches portal’s does, and an allocation opens as a window that reads first. A team’s account stays a page. Four specimens: Payees over the Ledger with a payee one level in; an allocation as a window that reads the bill first and whose pencil edits only its name and note; a team’s bill one level inside it; and one rule for every door (it opens where you are, and closing puts you back). Stage 4 — The club's public face

Walk §H · marketing truth

Home for a rep-only club (programs first, tournaments last and absent when none, the club's colours, a footer with contact); a Teams index and a Teams tab; the tryout funnel; the editor with section controls; the coach's public URL with a copy button; the same public checks on every page; the archive org check. Marketing: "coming soon" out when Stage 8 says so, the false "parent notifications" and "field bookings" lines removed, README and comparison table reconciled.

Stage 5 — Families
