Stage 6 — Venues, scheduling, permits

Rulings D3 D4 D5 first · walk §I

One venue book: a coach's place can be one of the club's venues; tournaments read their source venue; a cross-module clash check warns on every write. Venue Library gates and errors fixed. An internal read-only club calendar in org time. The venue book and clash check are shaped so permits (Stage 10) can plug in. Drawn 2026-10-08 (Mockups → Stage 6, beside 3d): seven specimens and thirteen asks, ratified 2026-10-08, every one as recommended (the seventh, one way to enter where an event is on every form, asked by the owner the same day). Built as two sessions: 6a the venue book, the clash check and the one Where field (CLUB_TIER_STAGE6A_BUILD_PROMPT.md), then 6b the club calendar and the Venue library (CLUB_TIER_STAGE6B_BUILD_PROMPT.md).

Stage 6c — One calendar: every schedule in the app, side by side (added 2026-10-09)

Added by the owner 2026-10-09 with the coach Schedule deep dive merged into this project · before the Stage 10 + 11 drawing session · its rulings come first; its builds don’t hold the release

The product has seven calendars — the coach’s schedule, the club calendar, house league’s schedule, the tournament admin’s schedule, the public league and tournament schedules, the family app — each designed on its own, and some copy parts from each other without the reason behind them (the club calendar’s phone Export and List, both fixed 2026-10-09, were copies of the coach schedule’s). One session lays every calendar side by side on a computer and a phone and settles one recipe (the views a calendar offers and what each means, the toolbar, the date row, how a booking reads, how a clash is marked, where Filter and Export sit) and a register of deliberate differences, each with its reason. Each screen’s own project builds its changes; the review rebuilds nothing itself. The coach’s desktop schedule (the deep dive’s stage 2: open on today, a Month that says what and when, one toolbar row) is drawn inside it, because the coach schedule is the pattern the others copy. The scheduler’s grid (Stage 11) is drawn on the recipe. Drawn and RATIFIED 2026-10-10 (Mockups → Stage 6c): nine calendars compared side by side with captures, a thirteen-line recipe and a register of what differs on purpose, the coach’s desk schedule and the club calendar drawn before and after, every other calendar’s delta handed to its owner, Stage 11’s grid as a specimen; all twenty asks and the design review’s eleven changes as recommended. Build prompt: CLUB_TIER_STAGE6C_BUILD_PROMPT.md (Part A, the three date defects, first). The Stage 10 + 11 session may open.

Stage 6d — Calendar feeds (the deep dive’s stage 4)

After 6c · before Stage 11 is built · doesn’t hold the release (recommended)

A coach subscribes once and their calendar stays current: a “Subscribe on this phone” row beside the download, every kind of event, cancelled ones marked cancelled. With it, the team-wide feed that has had no caller since September (D07) and the club calendar’s subscribable link (handed here by Stage 6’s Ask 10). Stage 11’s club slots reach families through the team’s feed, so the feed is settled first. A coach-scoped feed may need new storage, decided when drawn. Drawn 2026-10-11 and ratified the same day (Mockups → Stage 6d; plan §6 Stage 6d; build prompt CLUB_TIER_STAGE6D_BUILD_PROMPT.md): Subscribe behind the coach’s one Export and the phone’s calendar mark, and on the public team page’s Schedule line; one Subscribe window (three app doors, a link you can see again, what’s in it, how often, last read, Reset); the words every feed writes; every ask as recommended, with the last read once a day, a four-hour hint and the public feed cached; the club admin’s feed deferred and the family view untouched until counsel.

Stage 6e — The event form’s last corrections (the deep dive’s stage 5)

Re-read first · any gap in the sequence · doesn’t hold the release

The 2026-10-09 rulings already changed this form (the event window reads first and its pencil opens a held save; a change that tells families asks; a series edit asks its scope at the pencil), so “Edit details keeps its Save” is likely settled. Left to check: the practice’s More label, the series’ per-date opponent boxes taking the Opponent Picker, and an arrival after the start flagged.

Stage 7 — Tournaments in a club + one door to every family

Walk §J

The hub banner logic for a club; one-click "add my team" for a club org; tournament fees into the books by decision; one org-wide announcement door with a preview count, suppression, a send log and a cap. Drawn with it (merged 2026-10-09, the deep dive’s stage 3): the Coaches Portal’s Tournaments list and record given a proper phone pass, titled by the tournament, with a road to its games — shared with the free portal, and not holding the release.

Stage 8 — Release readiness

Go/no-go on the nine points

A Club browser suite on the fixture; admin club routes in the layout sweep; every club help article re-read; a demo decision; pricing and marketing drift check; the gate flip runbook and checkout verified; migrations on prod in order with functions verified; support posture and rollback runbook; the release and cohort shape logged.

Stage 9 — House league (its own release track)

Its own plan when it opens · D11 · may run alongside Stage 10

The trust-plan defects re-verified and closed; the standalone-plan coupling check; the ledger seam under D1's pattern; venues under Stage 6's book; confirms on one-click season changes; League Plus un-parked as the standalone plan.

Stage 10 — Permits & bookings (ruled in 2026-09-25; the release waits for it)

New feature · its own plan, PM brief and mockup session · walk §K

A permit is a record the club holds: venue, date range, weekly slots, cost and payee, the issuer's reference and document, and who it is for. Scheduling reads it — the clash check gains "is this slot inside a permit we hold?", the league generator and club calendar can offer permitted slots, a coach's event at a club venue shows the permit it sits in. Money reads it — a permit's cost can be cited by a budget line and allocated to teams. A per-permit view of used vs unused slots. Out of the first cut: requesting or paying for permits through the platform, municipal integrations, public booking. Drawn 2026-10-10 with Stage 11, RATIFIED 2026-10-11 (build prompt CLUB_PERMITS_BUILD_PROMPT.md) (Mockups → Stages 10 + 11; plan CLUB_PERMITS_AND_SCHEDULER_PLAN.md): Permits as a second view of the Venue library, a permit that reads first (its time, cost, budget line and use), the quiet “not inside a permit” line, a permit that prices its fields; all twenty-seven asks as recommended (Ask 4, which plans carry permits, is logged by /strategy before its gate is built).

Stage 11 — The club’s schedules: a scheduler (added 2026-10-08)

Added by the owner · ruled 2026-10-08 · drawn with Stage 10 in one session · the release waits for it · walk §L

A club admin hands out the club’s shared time (a dome’s winter hours, the pitching tunnel’s nights, house league’s practice slots): a few parameters in (which venue and facilities, when, which teams, how much each gets, and rules folded away until wanted), a draft out, adjusted by hand the way a tournament director adjusts a generated schedule, then finalized. Each schedule is kept by name (“Winter dome 2026–27”), reopened or copied next year, read as summaries (the whole dome, one team, one program) and sent to stakeholders (house league admins, each team’s coaches) with a preview and a send log; families see their team’s slots on its schedule. It hands out time, not game pairings. Ruled 2026-10-08: a club slot shows on a team’s schedule as “From the club”, read-only to the coach, who can hand it back (D3 amended narrowly, the tournament-game pattern); one model of the club’s time shared with permits, so Stages 10 and 11 are drawn together; owner and admin build it, a league admin for house league’s teams; time only; the release waits for it; League Plus and both Club bands carry it alike (logged with /strategy). Drawn 2026-10-10 with Stage 10, RATIFIED 2026-10-11 (build prompts CLUB_SCHEDULER_A_BUILD_PROMPT.md, the server, and CLUB_SCHEDULER_B_BUILD_PROMPT.md, the screens, after permits) (Mockups → Stages 10 + 11; plan CLUB_PERMITS_AND_SCHEDULER_PLAN.md): Schedules under Calendar, New schedule in the tournament generator’s frame, ranked drafts, a week grid with every open slot, fairness beside it, Send with a preview, changes sent as changes, a coach’s club slot and its hand-back, the time shared by percentage like money, a draft read day by day and exported before it is kept, a team’s days off, and the owner’s winter-dome flow walked end to end; all twenty-seven asks as recommended. 11c drawn 2026-10-12 and ratified the same day, all seven asks as recommended, the build starting once the dome walk (§300) is complete (Mockups → Stage 11c; plan §6c; build prompt CLUB_SCHEDULER_11C_BUILD_PROMPT.md): New schedule regrouped into three questions, rules as sentences with one Add a rule, Sharing a facility (named teams share; a shared slot is half a facility, its cost half as the owner ruled the same day), and Each team’s time (the same each week, or moved around). 11d drawn 2026-10-12, its nine asks open (Mockups → Stage 11d; plan §6d): a hand-back that asks for money back, from the owner’s direction while walking §300 W10. The coach ticks “Ask the club for $432.00 back” on Hand back; the club accepts or declines; accepting opens the time and takes the money off what the team still owes (a credit, new to club money), or makes a request to pay for what it had already paid. The club’s own changes settle the same way, and a hand-back never leaves the schedule waiting for a send.

Sequencing

Stage 1 before everything — no other walk is honest while admins and treasurers are tournament-only users. Stage 2 before 3 — the allocation loop needs teams, program years and the season rule. Stages 4, 5, 6, 7 are independent of each other and of 3. Stage 10 needs Stage 6's venue book and Stage 3's allocations, and the release waits for it, so Stage 8's go/no-go comes after Stages 3, 6 and 10 at the earliest. Stage 9 is its own release track. 2026-10-09: Stage 6c (one calendar) comes before the Stage 10 + 11 drawing session, because the scheduler’s grid is the club calendar’s week; 6d (feeds) follows 6c and lands before Stage 11 is built; 6e and the coach portal’s Tournaments (with Stage 7) fill gaps. None of the merged coach schedule work holds the release; only 6c’s rulings sit on its path.

Findings referenced on the map

A01 — Anyone but the owner is a tournament-only user

Admin and staff have no module permissions by default; the hub decides "tournament-only" from the member, not the plan, and redirects them into tournaments or an owner-only setup page that bounces them back. Stage 1, ruling D8.

A02 — The board cannot be staffed from the screen

Treasurer, registrar and league admin exist in the product but not in the invite or role pickers; saving another role quietly turns it into staff; help still tells owners to pick Treasurer. Stage 1.

A03 — A coach who coaches elsewhere cannot join a club's board

The membership policy counts the plumbing rows every coaching-staff invite writes, so the invite, the acceptance and a reinstatement all refuse. Contradicts the July account-model decision. Stage 1.

A05 — No way to buy Club

The billing shelf only opens an article; only Tournament Plus can be upgraded to; Club · Association appears on no customer surface; the team-cap error tells a club to upgrade with nowhere to go. Stage 1, ruling D7.

A07 — Coming back after cancelling restores nothing

Resubscribing restores only a plan-downgrade retention; the site stays hidden, tournaments stay archived, and the retention job later emails a paying customer that their window expired. Stage 1.

A08 — The Founding Season comp leaks onto Club

Every signup gets the comp; moving the org to Club does not revoke it; the billing page then says Club is free through 2027 beside a $219 card. Stage 1, ruling D6.

A09 — "Listed on /discover" is the master switch for the whole site

The checkbox writes the public flag, which hides the org home, the league pages and every link back to the org. The real directory flag has no control. Stage 1.

B01 — A new head coach must be invited as staff or admin

No Coach role exists to invite; the Coaches page assigns only existing active members; no email tells the coach they were assigned; between seasons a coach cannot be added at all. Stage 2, ruling D10.

B03 — Club teams have no season rollover

"Start next season" is standalone-only; the club's new program year is blank; a new year is blocked while one is active, so next season's tryouts cannot open until this season is marked complete — which locks every coach out. Stage 2.

B04 — Adopting a standalone portal orphans the team

The transfer routine was written when the team had 17 tables and never revised; it leaves behind the coach's access record and roughly 48 tables added since. The customer UI calls the rest "platform-assisted". Stage 2.

B05 — The coach portal never checks the plan

A club that downgrades keeps every team's full Premium portal while the downgrade copy says it shuts down. Stage 1.

B06 — Dead doors on the club side

"View roster" and two sidebar links go to pages that do not exist; the "Ungrouped" filter crashes the team list. Stage 0.

B08 — No cross-team oversight

Team cards answer roster, pending and families only; three different roster-count rules and two record rules across the club screens. Stage 2.

C01 — Two money-entry controls dead since June

The payee box on the ledger form and add-item / add-category on the budget form call routes that now require the org and get refused. Stage 0.

C03 — A treasurer cannot finish the allocation loop

The allocate wizard loads teams from rep-teams routes the treasurer cannot see, so the team list is empty; the reminder buttons are shown to treasurers and always refused. Stage 0 / 1.

C04 — Net position mixes team and league money into the club's figure

Every ledger counts and none is ever archived; there is no whole-club picture. Stage 3, ruling D1.

C05 — Headroom is budget minus at most 50 expenses

A club with more than fifty expense entries in a year is shown a wrong headline. Stage 3.

C07 — Money moves on one click with no reversal and a race

Approve is one click, the accounting entry is never linked so nothing can be reversed, two approvals can post two transfers, and a lost race leaves an orphaned transfer. Stage 3a.

C10 — The club cannot plan next year

Only the current year and years with lines can be chosen; allocation resolves the current calendar year only; no year-end exists while the coach side has close, settlement and carry-forward. Stage 3c, ruling D2.

C18 — Tournament money never reaches the books

Fees live on the team row; house-league fee entries are created on approval day, never voided, and can be revived. Stage 7 by decision.

D01 — Double-booking checks stop at module boundaries

Each module checks only itself; rep-team events check nothing. Stage 6.

D02 — The venue library refuses the person the scheduler sends there

Saving a venue needs a tournament permission a league admin lacks, and the page swallows the refusal. Stage 6.

D03 — No club calendar

Nothing spans teams; the admin's team schedule shows device time and buckets days by UTC. Stage 6, ruling D5.

D04 — The admin cannot add a game

By the franchise ruling coaches own the schedule; admin writes were removed deliberately. Stage 6, ruling D3.

D06 — Permits do not exist

No table, route, page or plan; the homepage says clubs manage field bookings. Stage 6, ruling D4.

D05 — The Venue library’s guard, rename, copy and doors

Delete is final and checks nothing, and house league’s bookings lose the venue; no facility rename on the page; copy names tournaments and house league only; the Organization tile has no plan gate. Stage 6b, Ask 9.

D07 — The team-wide calendar feed is dead

Nothing makes its link; the export’s “STUB” header was trued 2026-09-25; help still promises a subscribable link. Ask 10: to the schedule deep dive’s stage 4.

S6-01 — The release target’s clashes are between its own teams

A rep club with no house league double-books between its own teams; the check covers rep × rep. Ask 3.

S6-02 — The coach demo double-books its own diamond every week

Every home game and practice of the demo’s teams is seeded on one diamond. /demos, once 6a ships.

S6-03 — The tournament’s own overlap refusal is a browser rule

Two windows refuse; drag, the rain-delay shift, the generator, the playoffs and the server skip it. Tournament Stage 3.

S6-04 — A tournament venue’s library link is written once and read by nothing

A clone and import-from-past drop it; a second import duplicates; the wizard searches other tournaments’ copies. 6a keeps the link; Tournament Stage 5 redraws the wizard.

S6-05 — A series edit leaves each date’s place link behind

The words change on every date, the link on none. 6a.

S6-06 — The tournament mirror writes into a team’s schedule on every read

A mirrored game is the tournament’s booking; the check skips it. 6a.

S6-07 — Nearly half of rep events have no end

119 of 259 on dev; counted as 90 minutes. Ask 3.

S6-08 — Deleting a library venue strips house league’s bookings

Archive when anything books it. 6b, Ask 9.

S6-09 — A failed library load reads as an empty library

Say so, with Try again. 6b.

S6-10 — Any member can write venues directly

The database’s rules allow it; members read, the server writes. 6b.

S6-11 — The Organization page’s Venues tile has no plan gate

And a second name. 6b.

S6-12 — The public league schedule groups weeks by the server’s clock

UTC on the host. Ask 8, in 6b.

S6-13 — No org records a time zone or a province

A platform item before the first club outside Eastern time.

C6-01 — The coach’s date arrows skip a month at month-end, and drift east of UTC

Read and run 2026-10-10. The Schedule’s arrows step from a date on the device’s clock: from the 29th to the 31st the month arrow lands two months on (on Oct 31, › opens December) in every time zone, Eastern included; east of UTC every press lands a day short, so a week repeats after five presses. The arrows have no names for a screen reader, and the Week’s arrows don’t move the phone Month’s chosen day. Proposed: Fix now, one small commit (Ask 17): step by the calendar (the club calendar’s and the admin team schedule’s arithmetic already do), name the arrows, keep the chosen day on the grid. Before Oct 29.

C6-02 — The coach’s Overview shows a tournament a day early

Read and run 2026-10-10. The live tournament card parses a bare date as midnight in UTC and formats it on the device, so every time zone in the Americas reads the day before (“Oct 9 - Oct 11, 2026” for Oct 10–12, with a hyphen). The Tournaments tile and the quiet-week card read a day early east of Eastern. Proposed: Fix now with C6-01: the zone helpers, and the one range spelling (“Oct 10–12, 2026”).

C6-03 — The free coach schedule reads the device’s clock

Read 2026-10-10. The free portal’s schedule formats every date and time with the device’s own zone, so a coach whose phone is set elsewhere reads other hours. It is the one schedule left on the device clock (R5). Proposed: Fix now with C6-01. No project owns the free portal’s schedule.

C6-04 — The public league shows a postponed game as on, and hides a cancelled one

Read and captured 2026-10-10. The page’s read drops cancelled games, and a postponed game keeps its old date and time with no word, so a family can turn up for a game that isn’t happening. It also has no place and no today. Proposed: Stage 9 (house league’s public face), drawn on specimen 3; the state words sooner if house league ships before Stage 9.

C6-05 — A team’s schedule (admin) is a second, older copy of the coach’s views

Captured 2026-10-10. Gapped cards with a rail (the coach’s pre-2026-09-16 list), Won / Lost where the coach says Win / Loss, no score; at 1440 the Week’s names spill into the next day’s column; Month’s “+N more” is plain text; a phone gets seven sideways columns with the names cut off; the window still has Done. Proposed: The 6c build (Ask 14): the page draws the coach’s views with every write absent.

C6-06 — The tournament’s Day shows no clash on its rows

Read 2026-10-09 build. Another program’s booking on a field is 6a’s amber line inside the game window and the timeline’s cross note; the Day’s rows show neither. A41’s recommended option asked for “the clash marks the same”. Proposed: A finding for the tournament redesign: the amber line under a row’s where-line.

C6-07 — The public tournament: a forfeit shows nothing, the calendar file uses the device’s clock

Read 2026-10-10. A forfeit gets no badge and no score; “Add My Games to Calendar” writes its times in the device’s zone; the tournament home says Unofficial for every submitted score even when the event doesn’t require finalizing. Proposed: Tournament redesign; the calendar file’s clock with 6d.

C6-08 — The scorekeeper opens on the device’s day

Read 2026-10-10. The scorekeeper’s default day is the device’s calendar day, while its overdue check uses the event’s; a volunteer east of the event sees tomorrow after 7 p.m. Eastern. Proposed: Tournament redesign.

C6-09 — The coach’s tournament record decides LIVE by its own rule

Read 2026-10-10. LIVE is “a submitted score, today”, not the shared rule the public screens use: an unscored game in progress isn’t live, and a submitted score stays LIVE all day. Proposed: Stage 7, where the record is drawn.

C6-10 — One choice of view, three looks

Captured 2026-10-10. On the coach’s schedule the chosen view is the portal’s olive; on the club calendar and the admin team schedule, the same toolbar’s switch is the admin kit’s black fill; the tournament’s schedule chooses its view with the olive View pill, a dropdown. Proposed: Ask 13: the olive face chooses what is read (2026-10-07): a switch with the portal’s olive where three views fit, the olive View pill for four or more (the tournament’s View pill is the third look today).

C6-11 — Three answers to “which clock?”

Read 2026-10-10. The club calendar says “Times in Eastern time.” (written into the page, not read from the club’s zone); the public tournament says “All times are local.”; every other calendar says nothing. Proposed: Ask 10: one sentence, read from the club’s zone, wherever a reader may sit outside it.

C6-12 — A41’s “one shape” wasn’t built, and “whichever builds first” doesn’t pick it

Read 2026-10-10 from the code and the commits. The club calendar (Oct 9, 6:18 p.m.) was committed before the tournament’s Day (9:54 p.m.), but the Day wore the admin kit’s row (Club Stage 2, Sep 29), older than both, and neither imports the other. The club calendar draws a booking three ways (the List’s table, the Week card, the phone card); none is the kit’s row. Proposed: Ask 5: the shared part is the row both already have a copy of (the portal’s row and the kit’s row, one recipe); the club calendar’s List moves onto it. The Day stays as built.

C6-13 — Stage 11’s draft grid can’t be the club calendar’s Week

Read 2026-10-10 against the plan’s Stage 11 shape (“a draft grid (facility × week, the club calendar’s Week view)”). The Week stacks bookings as cards by day; it has no hours and no empty slots, so a free slot has nothing to be. Proposed: Ask 18: the grid takes the Timeline’s shape (facilities down, the hours in each day) and wears the recipe’s lines. Stage 11 draws it.

C6-14 — Month grids start on Sunday; every Week on Monday

Read and captured 2026-10-10. The coach’s and the admin team’s Month start on Sunday; their Weeks, the club calendar’s Week and Month, house league and the public league start on Monday; the public tournament’s jump list groups weeks from Sunday. Proposed: Ask 2: Monday, everywhere.

C6-15 — House league’s “Week” is a season

Read and captured 2026-10-10. House league’s Week view is the selected division’s whole season in week groups, and its List the same season as a table. Proposed: Stage 9 (Ask 1, Ask 15).

C6-16 — The club calendar hides cancelled and postponed bookings

Read 2026-10-10 (a build-time choice in 6b, not drawn or asked). A called-off game and a never-booked slot look the same on the president’s week. Proposed: Ask 9: shown, struck through and dimmed, never a clash.

S6D-01 — Nobody receives a feed today

Counted read-only on 2026-10-11. No team on either database is at Public link (dev 0 of 34, production 0 of 6: every team is at Families), and no feed link of either kind has ever been made. The only connected families are the coach demo’s twelve seeded guardians (one team, on both databases) plus one real one on dev; no new one can connect while the guardian switch is off. Production holds one club that can open a club calendar, and it is the demo. Plan: Recorded, not an ask: 6d designs doors for an audience that doesn’t exist yet. It changes the risk, not the design: nothing a customer uses moves, so the build can retire the never-used team-wide link outright.

S6D-02 — A feed link can be shown only once

Links are stored only as a fingerprint, so the server can never show one again. The family view’s Subscribe therefore makes a new link on every press, and the button then reads “New link”: pressing it on a second device silently stops the subscription already in the first. The team-wide link’s function makes a new link on every call too (named “ensure”, it rotates), so a public page could not show it without stopping every other subscriber on each visit. That is likely why it was never wired (D07). Plan: Ask 8: a personal link is signed, so the server can rebuild it for its owner and a database read alone can’t; a counter retires it on Reset. The public team page needs no secret at all (Ask 3).

S6D-03 — The feed counts its readers by address, across every feed

240 reads an hour per caller address, one budget for every feed on the platform, failing open if the counter is down. Calendar services fetch subscriptions from shared servers, so one Google server polling many teams’ feeds shares one budget; past it, every one of them is refused, and the calendars simply stop updating with nothing to tell anyone. Plan: Ask 10, as ruled: count per feed, writing nothing on a good read; keep failing open.

S6D-04 — A link that stops answers “not found”, and calendar apps keep the last copy

Every reason a feed stops (a revoked family, a closed schedule, a cancelled club) answers “not found”. A calendar app that can’t read a feed generally keeps the last copy it read, so the old events stay in that calendar, frozen: a game moved afterwards never moves, and a team that closed its schedule stays in strangers’ calendars. Plan: Ask 9: a link that was genuinely issued and has stopped answers with an empty calendar under its name, so its events leave; a link never issued stays “not found”. The build walks it in Google, Apple and Outlook.

S6D-05 — The coach’s download is narrower than the coach’s screen

The coach’s Schedule shows tryout days (to a coach who runs tryouts) and the tournament’s own games not yet on the team’s list (an overlay), but the Calendar file writes only the team’s events. Nothing on either database is copied from a tournament onto a team’s schedule, so every tournament game a coach sees today reaches them as an overlay. Plan: Ask 2: the coach’s feed carries both; the download follows in the same build.

S6D-06 — There are no staff-only events

An event has no visibility of its own: a family reads every event of the live season that the coach puts on the schedule. The prompt’s shape assumed a coach’s feed would add staff-only events. Plan: Ask 2, corrected: what a coach’s feed adds is the tryout days, the notes and uniform, and the organizer’s games. A staff-only kind of event would be a new ask, not 6d’s.

S6D-07 — The family feed’s words are not the recipe’s

“13U AAA — Practice”; always “vs” (36 of production’s live games are away); “Arrive by 17:30”, the stored string (one dev event stores “5:45 PM”, so both forms exist); a cancelled event dropped; three neutral-site games on production; no zone, though a calendar may sit elsewhere. Plan: The feed recipe F1–F10 (specimen 5), from 6c’s ruling on what a feed carries.

S6D-08 — An outside tournament writes as a two-hour block

An outside tournament is a span of days with no time (one on each database). Every calendar export writes it as a two-hour block at its start; the deep dive left this to its stage 4. Plan: F4: an all-day entry across its days, in every feed and the download.

S6D-09 — The public team page checks less than the feed

The page shows a Public link schedule for a club that has cancelled; the feed refuses it (D07, still true). Dev holds three real teams in a cancelled club, all at Families, so nothing shows today. The plan’s F06 already asks every public page to make the same checks. Plan: Ask 10: the page’s schedule, its Subscribe button and the feed ask one question, so they can’t disagree.

S6D-10 — Help promises the link “for a future release”; the family door is an emoji

The exports help’s “Do exports update automatically?” answer and its search text say a live subscribable calendar URL is “planned for a future release”. The family view’s door is a 📅 emoji, a sentence, a button, and a raw address with no Copy and no app door. Plan: Ask 10 and Part B: help rewritten with the build; the family door becomes the shared window.

S6D-11 — No refresh hint, and no name when empty

The file sends no refresh hint (Outlook and Apple read one; Google ignores it), and a feed with no events carries no calendar name, so a team subscribed before its first event shows a generic name. Plan: F8: a four-hour refresh hint (owner 2026-10-11: one hour would bring Apple and Outlook back hourly) and the calendar’s name, always; help says Google can take up to a day.

S6D-12 — When a season closes, its events leave every subscribed calendar

The family feed reads the live season only. When a season closes (or the team starts its next one), the feed’s events change wholesale, and a subscribed calendar drops the season’s past games at its next check. Nobody is told. Plan: Ask 9: keep it (a closed season is one page, by ruling; a feed is an instrument), and say it in the window: “This season only. When it’s closed, its events leave your calendar.”

S6D-13 — The club calendar’s read is built for one page view

The club calendar reads at most 42 days at a time and works out the clashes over the club’s whole pool on each read. A feed polled by calendar services all day needs a wider window and has no use for clash pairs. Plan: Ask 4: the club feed reads four weeks back to six months ahead and carries the bookings without clash lines; the clash check stays on the page. Deferred from the first build (owner 2026-10-11).

S6D-14 — The family door works, for nobody

The per-family feed and its door work for any connected guardian; a guardian connects only through the coach’s invite, which the guardian switch refuses while it is off. So the door is live code with no reachable audience (production: the demo’s twelve, who never pressed it). Plan: Ask 3: drawn as it will be and tagged; the build may swap it to the shared window, which changes nothing anyone can reach until counsel signs off.

P11-01 — “The Timeline’s shape” names two different layouts

Read in the code and a capture, 2026-10-10. The built tournament Timeline is one day at a time, with the facilities across as columns and the hours down; a column exists only where a game stands, and an empty slot is never drawn. The ruled words (6c Ask 18, the register’s R3) say “fields down, time across”. The drawing the owner saw, 6c specimen 4, is a third thing: facility rows, a column per day, each day’s slots in clock order. Plan: Ask 12: the grid takes specimen 4’s layout (what the owner saw), and the Timeline’s behaviour (drag with a preview, a refusal with its reason, Undo), not its axes. The standard’s R3 is reworded after the ruling (/design, Stage 8).

P11-02 — Nothing in the tournament generator is shared yet

Its own header says so: “The frame is tagged for Club Stage 11’s scheduler (A40); nothing here is shared yet.” Its engine assigns two-sided matchups to slots of one length, ranked by per-game measures (rest, back-to-backs, field moves), and its edge-slot rule penalises any slot from 5 p.m. on, which is prime time for a weeknight practice. Plan: Ask 5: the scheduler wears the generator’s frame and look (the two-step wide window, the ranked cards, one statement, Undo, the publish window’s “who is told”) and builds its own engine and grid. Lifting the frame into one shared window part is a shared ask to the tournament redesign, with no change the tournament can see.

P11-03 — “From the club” already means money

In the coach’s Money › Club tab, a request the club pays reads “From the club” (and “To club” the other way), in the panel, the exports and help. A practice reading “From the club” would give one phrase two meanings in one portal. Plan: Ask 16: the mirror’s own construction, “From Winter dome 2026–27 · the club’s schedule”, naming the schedule as the tournament mirror names its tournament. /marketing words it.

P11-04 — The clash rule would misread the club’s own slots

Two teams sharing one lane in one slot are two bookings on one facility at one time: the rule calls that “booked by”. The “permit hook” left for a third clash kind assumes no caller changes, but the callers filter the two kinds by name and the calendar counts pairs, and a booking against a permit is not a pair. And the pool holds the club’s venues only, so it can’t say a team has an away game that day. Plan: Rows from one club slot never clash with each other, and the calendar reads a shared slot as one booking. “Not inside a permit” is built as its own answer beside the pair rule (Ask 3). The scheduler’s “never on a team’s game day” reads each team’s whole schedule.

P11-05 — The tournament mirror writes when a schedule is opened

A published tournament game reaches a team only when the coach’s or the admin’s schedule is read (a sync before the read, debounced 10 seconds). Copied, a club slot would reach the team, the club calendar, the clash check and the feed only once someone opened that team’s schedule. Plan: Sending writes the bookings, once, when the schedule is sent (screen 9). The mirror’s other rules carry over: the server refuses a change to the slot’s time, place and name; the coach keeps their own parts.

P11-06 — A team’s event belongs to one season

Every rep event carries its season, and the family feed reads only the active or draft season. A January dome slot sent in December lands in whatever season the team is running then; a team with no season running can’t take one; a team that starts its next season mid-schedule would leave its upcoming slots on a closed season, which becomes one page. Plan: Ask 15: a slot lands in the team’s running season at the send; Who lists only teams with a season running, as New allocation does; starting a team’s next season carries its upcoming club slots into the new one.

P11-07 — House league can’t hold a club slot today

A practice is made by hand and can then only be cancelled; it records no source and no maker; only the owner and a league admin may write one (a club admin is refused on every write); and no family sees a practice anywhere (the public league pages read games only; no feed; no notice). Plan: Ask 6: a practice made by a schedule reads as the schedule’s and changes only there; it needs a link to its slot and a writer the schedule runs. Recommended with Stage 9, where League Plus un-parks; the first cut hands time to rep teams.

P11-08 — Nothing sends to staff, there is no facility contact, and no email carries an attachment

No door reaches every rep coach, every league admin or an outside contact; venues and payees hold no email; every PDF is drawn in the browser and no email sends a file. The one full send pattern is Stage 3a’s reminders. Plan: Ask 7 and Ask 9: the send copies the reminders’ window and log; the venue gains a bookings contact; the dome’s office reads the schedule in the email body for now.

P11-09 — A change that reached teams at once would land half-done

The plan’s shape said an edit marks the schedule “changed since sent” and Send the changes tells the teams, without saying when the bookings themselves change. If each move reached the teams at once, a rearrangement in progress (swap two, then move a third) would sit on families’ calendars half finished, before anyone was told. Plan: Ask 14: the teams keep what they were sent; Send the changes applies and tells together; until then the page lists what changed and Undo still works.

P11-10 — The split by hours already exists

New allocation’s By sessions split is already weighted by each team’s count, and the count can be any positive number. (The data dictionary still says it is entered by hand; that line is stale.) Plan: Ask 8b: a cost split by the hours each team got is By sessions with hours filled in from a sent schedule: words and a prefill, later.

P11-11 — On production, facility time is the teams’ money

No customer holds a venue or a house league on production. Coaches budget their own dome time ($10,000.00 on one team), diamond rentals ($6,000.00) and cage time ($4,983.30), and no rep event on either database names a dome, cage, tunnel or gym. Plan: Recorded, not an ask: the stages assume the club holds the time, which is right for a club; a team that rents its own time keeps doing what it does today.

P11-12 — A move in a weekly schedule needs a “which weeks” answer

The grid shows a real week, one of twelve. A drag has no way to say whether it moves this week’s slot or every week’s. The coach’s repeating-event pencil asks exactly this (2026-10-09). Plan: Ask 13: the drop asks, with the pencil’s three rows (This week only · This & later weeks · Every week); Undo takes back whichever was chosen.

S11C-01 — Teams at once is the whole schedule’s number

New schedule’s Teams at once (1 to 4) sits in The time and applies to every slot: the generator gives each slot that many seats and any team can take any seat; the slot window refuses one team more than the number. Set it to 2 and every team shares, seniors included. Plan: Ask 1: sharing becomes a rule about the teams named (Sharing a facility: teams or groups, how many at once); every other team keeps a facility to itself, and Teams at once leaves The time.

S11C-02 — Bill splits a shared slot; Fair shares counts it whole

Bill the teams prices each team’s minutes as a slot’s minutes × its facility’s share ÷ the teams in it, so two teams in one slot already pay half each. The generator’s results count each team the slot’s whole minutes, and each seat as one slot toward a share, so Fair shares and the drafts read a team that shares every slot as getting twice the time it pays for. Plan: Owner, 2026-10-12: a shared slot counts as half a facility from a cost perspective (ruled; how Bill works today). Ask 3: count it half for the shares too, so the bill and the fairness read one number.

S11C-03 — Each team keeps its place; only prime time rotates

Week by week the generator prefers what each team had before: the same facility, the same start, the same day. “Rotate it weekly” (prime time’s Share setting) and the “Prime time rotated” draft move prime-time slots only, and only where prime time is set. The dome has no prime time, so every Sunday comes out identical (the owner’s capture, 2026-10-12). Plan: Ask 4: Each team’s time, The same each week (today, the default) or Moved around (start and facility taken in turn, days kept). Ask 5: it answers prime time’s keep-or-rotate too.

S11C-04 — Prime time is set in Rules and shared in Who

Prime time’s hours and its Keep / Rotate live in Rules; “Prime time: Shared the same way · Shared evenly by team” lives in Who, and how much, and appears only once hours are set and the split is By percentage, so a choice in a later card makes a control appear in an earlier one. Plan: Ask 5: prime time whole in Who, and how much, its hours and how it is shared side by side.

S11C-05 — Rules draws every kind, empty

Opened, Rules draws three headings with Add doors, two “No limit” dropdowns, prime time and three ticks whether or not the club uses any of them: about thirteen controls for the dome’s one rule. The folded line already writes the rules as sentences (“9U AA, 11U AA finish by 8:00 p.m.”); the open card does not. Plan: Ask 6: each rule reads as its sentence and opens in place; one Add a rule menu for every kind; the three safeguards keep their ticks under Always.

S11C-06 — A half facility already counts half

A permit’s half field carries a weight of one half: the fairness swap evens out what each team’s time is worth with it, and Bill prices with it. A shared half field would be a quarter each. Plan: Not drawn: the build refuses a sharing rule on a half facility, or counts a quarter. Recommended: refuse it, and say so in the rule’s sentence.

S11D-01 — Hand back asks nothing about money

Hand back which practices? offers This practice only · This & future · All practices and lands at once: the team leaves the slots, an untouched practice is deleted (one with notes or attendance stays, struck through), the builders get a bell. No money is asked for or said. Plan: Ask 1: a tick, Ask the club for $X back, worked out from the bill. Ask 2: with it, the hand-back waits for the club.

S11D-02 — After a hand-back the page asks for a send it never offers

A hand-back marks a final schedule Changed since sent on purpose (build question B settles its money at the next Send the changes), but the page shows Send the changes only when the club changed a team’s time. After walk §300 W10 the page read “4 changes since you sent it” and “Send the changes to put these on their schedules” with no button, and the sentence is false for a hand-back: the team already has it. Plan: Ask 9: a hand-back never makes the schedule Changed since sent; its money settles at the answer (Ask 5), not at a send.

S11D-03 — The money a hand-back frees is told to nobody

Send the changes measures again every team that handed time back: 15U AA, 21 Sundays of 25, is owed $432.00 back, and the figure is written to the send log. A changes send emails only the teams whose practices it changes, so the hand-back team is never in it, and the send window shows owed-back only for a team it emails. Plan: Asks 5 and 8: the money is settled when the club answers, and told in the answer.

S11D-04 — Nothing can lower what a team owes

A bill’s terms never change (Ask 7b): its shares, payments and teams have no writer. Club money reaches a team only through a request the coach files and the club approves, and paying the team never lowers the team’s Outstanding. No credit, waiver or write-off exists in club money. Plan: Ask 6: a credit row against the bill, the bill itself unchanged; every figure that reads a bill reads billed less credited.

S11D-05 — Fair shares’ Bill and the team’s bill disagree

Fair shares prices each team’s time as it stands: after the hand-back, 15U AA $2,268.00 (21 Sundays). 15U AA’s bill on Money › Club still reads $2,700.00, and nothing says which is owed. Plan: Ask 6: once credits exist, the Bill column reads the bill less its credits plus its corrections, so the two agree; a hand-back without money keeps its note.

S11D-06 — A club move is told and left to the coach

At Send the changes, a team that loses time is told “is owed $108.00 back: its coach asks for it on Money › Club” (build question B, ruled 2026-10-11, “Bill gains, show losses”); the coach must file the request by hand, and the club then approves it. Plan: Ask 8: the club’s own change credits the team (or makes a request to pay) as part of the send, the same way an accepted hand-back does.

The whole area reached production without its owner walks. Stage 5.

The next read re-mints a ghost person for the merged address, who can be proposed again and messaged at the old address. Stage 5.

E02 — A changed guardian email strands the child

The child stays with the old person and messages go to the old address; the new address becomes a stranger. Stage 5.

E03 — Family money disagrees with the Money hub

Paid and unpaid are read from a stamp that only exists when an installment is fully paid, so partial payments vanish. Stage 5.

E04 — The export overclaims

It says "everything this organization holds" and carries a page's worth. Stage 5.

F01 — The tryouts card loops home

It links to a teams route that is only a redirect; the tryout's own address is already loaded and unused. Stage 0.

F02 — Rep teams are publicly invisible

No index, no link from anywhere, not in the sitemap or search. Stage 4.

F03 — The home page is tournament-first

An empty "no active tournaments" block leads the page fifty weeks a year. Stage 4.

F06 — Public team and tryout pages skip the checks other pages make

A cancelled or private club keeps serving team pages and tryout forms until the family submits. Stage 4.

F07 — Any org's archive can be shown under another org's name

The archive page loads by id alone. Stage 0.

F10 — Marketing promises what does not exist

Coming soon, parent notifications, field bookings, invoicing, reconciliation, a stale README price. Stage 4 / 8.

G01 — A "first tournament setup" banner forever

It shows whenever a club has no tournament and links to the house-league wizard. Stage 7.

G02 — No way to message every family

Tournament comms reach registered teams' coaches; league broadcast is per season; coach announcements per team; Families one household at a time. Stage 7.

G03 — The club's own team enters its own event in two steps

One-click works for coach-portal orgs only. Stage 7.

H01 — Nothing proves the club side works

No club browser suite, no admin routes in the layout sweep, no club demo, a fixture with two people and no teams. Stage 8.

I01 — A tenant-boundary hole in house league

Draft and placement routes accept division, registration and team ids from the request and return or rewrite other clubs' registrations, guardian contacts included. Stage 0 security sweep.

I02 — The admin is told about the wrong registrations

The "new registration" notice fires on a manual add, never on a parent's submission. Stage 9.

I04 — Deletes silently cascade

Deleting a team or division deletes its games and results; season changes fire in one click. Stage 9.

Stage 3c · findings drawn on the mockups

Headings for every finding a Stage 3c specimen flags that the lists above did not already carry (drawn 2026-10-07, from the code read that day). C10 and C17 are above; their 3c re-reading is in the finding's window.

S3C-01 — The year is worked out in a dozen places, not one

Three definitions read the year, nine screen readings work it out by hand (two from UTC timestamps), and the gate, the seed and the tests hard-code January. 3b's note said one place. The build routes every reading through one definition. Specimen 2.

S3C-02 — By period's quarters are calendar quarters

A September year would read five part-quarters. The club's quarters start at its first month; the coach's are unchanged. Specimen 2.

S3C-03 — The payee report matches a team season's number to the club year's

A year named 2025–26 has no single number; the build lists a team with a season numbered for either calendar year the club's year touches. Specimen 7.

S3C-04 — A season stores no dates

A year number, a name and a status; its start is its row's creation time and its "close date" is its last change. Nothing in 3c asks a season for its dates. Read first.

S3C-05 — An unpaid club bill leaves the coach's Club tab when its season rolls over

The Club tab reads the working season's bills; after the roll the old bill is on no live coach screen except a lane whose door leads back to the tab. A September year makes it ordinary. Ask 8b, specimen 8.

S3C-06 — "Ledgers archive at year-end" is the wrong goal

Nothing archives a book, and a club book runs across years. A year-end locks dates; archiving a finished tournament's book is Stage 7's. Ask 8a.

S3C-07 — Four corrections change a line where it sits

Undo, Reverse, Void and clearing a cheque would each move a closed year's locked figures. Refused on a closed year's line, pointing at Reopen. Ask 8d, specimen 3.

S3C-08 — A year can't stay a four-digit number

A change of first month makes two years share a number however it is keyed. The build's migration adds a row per club year. Not drawn.

S3C-09 — New allocation offers a team's closed seasons

Every season, worded with the database's status, and the server checks only that it is the team's. Only open seasons, under the word Season; the server refuses a closed one. Specimen 6.

S3C-10 — The payee window opens straight into an editable name

No reading state, and the report is a page one level down. The window reads first with the report as its body. Ask 7, specimen 7.

S3C-11 — A late payment of an old season’s club bill lands in the closed season

Found writing the build prompts (2026-10-07): the coach’s register counts a club bill’s payment in the bill’s season, so a payment after that season closed moves a closed season’s figures. Ruled the same day: the season running when the payment is recorded carries it; a past season is adjusted by reopening it (only while no season is running) and recording the payment there.

Stage 11a — the club scheduler, its screens (part B): Schedules under Calendar, New schedule started from a permit, three ranked drafts, a schedule’s page with Fair shares and moves by hand, Bill the teams, Send for review and Finalize, Changed since sent, and on the coach’s side the review card, a practice from the schedule, Hand back and the Budget’s callout — is walked as fifteen walks (ledger §300), all owed: the owner’s dome flow, end to end. Built 2026-10-11 and through /simplify, /review (high-risk) and /design. The test club starts with no schedule: walk 1 builds Winter dome · Sundays from the Winter dome 2026–27 permit, and every later walk reads what the earlier ones made, so go in order. Walks 5, 7 and 9 send (to the test club’s .local addresses) and walk 10 hands practices back; none of it is undone in the walk.

Stage 10a — permits, the time the club holds: the Venue library's Permits view, a permit that reads first, Add permit with what each field costs, Renew, the venue's Permits section and bookings contact, the quiet line on every form that asks where and in the club calendar, a budget line's Pays for and the use workbook — is walked as thirteen short walks (ledger §296), all owed. Built 2026-10-11 and through /simplify and /review; the test club has its two permits (Fall diamonds 2026, Winter dome 2026–27) from --club-permits. Walks 3, 4 and 10 write test data and undo it in the walk; walks 5 and 6 press Cancel; the rest only read. Go in any order.

Stage 6b — the club calendar (every program’s week in one read-only place, with its clashes marked and counted), the Venue library redesigned (who can change it, a venue that reads first, rename, Archive and Delete) and weeks grouped in the club’s time — is walked as nine short walks (ledger §288): walks 1 to 6 passed 2026-10-09. During walk 6 the owner ruled that Archive needs no pinned row of its own: Archive, Bring back and a payee’s Merge now end the window’s body beside Delete, so walk 7’s first, seventh and eighth steps and walk 8’s first step were reworded the same day. Walk 4 passed on the first layout; the owner then moved Export up into the Filter row on a phone, and then took List off the phone’s View drawer, so its steps 2, 3 and 6 were reworded the same day and are owed a re-check: on a phone, Filter and Export’s icon share the row under the title and the icon opens the menu, and the View drawer offers Week and Month. Walks 1 to 4 only read. Walks 5 to 9 write test data and each puts back what it changes, except that walk 8 deletes the venue walk 5 adds, so walk 5 goes first. The rest go in any order.

Stage 6a — the club’s venues, the one clash check and one Venue field on every form that asks where — is walked as eight short walks (ledger §284), all passed 2026-10-09. Walk 4 follows walk 3 (it edits the series walk 3 makes); walks 1, 3, 6 and 7 write test data, so each can be walked once; the rest go in any order.

Stage 3d — the last club money pages become windows: Payees over the Ledger (from Tools, and from inside an entry), one allocation window every door opens, an allocation’s name and note, a closed year’s allocation, the old addresses and a phone — is walked as eight short walks (ledger §285), all passed 2026-10-09. Each tests one job and is signed off on its own. Walks 3 and 5 write test data (a payee merge, an allocation’s new name and note), so each can be walked once; walk 5 goes after walk 4, whose steps name Diamond fees 2026 as it is now. The rest go in any order.

Stage 3c — the club’s fiscal year: setting it, every tab reading it by name, closing and reopening it, a closed year read in place, the year that opens, the year-end papers, New allocation from a line and from Allocations, a payee’s window and the coach’s earlier-season bill — is walked as eleven short walks (ledger §283), all owed. Each one tests one job, says what it’s for before you start, and is signed off on its own — a walk can pass while another is still open. Walks 4, 5, 6 and 7 go in that order: walk 4 reopens 2025–26 and backdates a missed cheque, walk 5 closes it again, and walks 6 and 7 read what that leaves. The rest go in any order. Walks 1, 4, 5, 8 and 9 write test data, and so does walk 6’s last step, so each can be walked once. After them, Stage 3b’s walk 13 (the coach’s Ledger gaining a Category filter, ledger §280) and walk 14 (Item following Category on both Ledgers, ledger §281) are still owed.
